stories.title: Donegal All-Ireland winner James McHugh dies in crash
stories.summary: Former Donegal 1992 All-Ireland winning football star James McHugh died in a road traffic collision in Co Cavan yesterday afternoon. The Cill Chartha native, who was in his early 60s, was in a collision involving a car and a van on the N3 at Drummallaght, between Virginia and Cavan town. A woman, also aged in her 60s who was a passenger in the car, was seriously injured and was airlifted to Beaumont Hospital for treatment. The driver of the van, a man in his 50s, was taken to hospital to be treated for minor injuries.

stories.title: Fans to welcome home Cork's All-Ireland camogie winners
stories.summary: The newly-crowned All-Ireland Senior Camogie champions will be welcomed back to Cork today with a special homecoming event. A second-half surge saw the Rebels dethrone Galway by 2-14 to 0-19 at Croke Park yesterday in what was another gripping and physical final between the two current heavyweights of the game. Ger Manley's side will kick off their first full day as All-Ireland champions with the traditional visit to Children's Health Ireland at Temple Street this morning. Children, parents and medical staff will get the opportunity to see the O'Duffy Cup - lifted by Cork for the 31st time yesterday - and meet with players and management.

stories.title: Call over access to drug to treat Friedreich's Ataxia
stories.summary: Sinn Féin Leader Mary Lou McDonald has called on the Government to ensure families affected by Friedreich's Ataxia can access drugs to treat it. Deputy McDonald said that the drug, Skyclarys, is "scheduled for consideration at a meeting on Tuesday, but the worry is that it will be referred on to yet another committee, another group for another round of consultation and decision". Friedreich's Ataxia is a rare inherited neurological condition that progressively damages the nervous system, affecting mobility, balance, and coordination. Clinical trials suggest Skyclarys - the first and only EU-authorised pharmaceutical treatment for the rare condition - could slow the progression of symptoms. The treatment is already publicly funded in a number of European countries.

stories.title: Vertiv to create 300 jobs in the northwest
stories.summary: Technology manufacturer Vertiv has announced plans for a major expansion of its operations in Co Donegal that is set to create 300 jobs in the northwest. The company, a global leader in critical digital infrastructure, said it will be submitting an application to Donegal County Council for an additional 7,000 square metres of space at its Letterkenny facility. Vertiv said plans to expand its manufacturing and testing footprint are driven by growing demand for infrastructure solutions supporting AI, colocation and hyperscale data centre deployments. Hyperscale data centres are often associated with big data-producing companies, while colocation is a practice where a business rents space in a third-party data centre.

stories.title: Police seek charges over Bangkok bar fire that killed 37
stories.summary: Thai police intend to charge the owner of a Bangkok bar with six offences, including negligence, over a fire last month that killed 37 people, the lead investigator has said. Suvicha Salaibatr, the owner of the popular Rong Beer Na Lad Phrao restaurant and bar, was among dozens of people hospitalised when a blaze engulfed his venue on the evening of 12 July. "We issued an arrest warrant last week against him on six charges" including negligence causing death, serious injury, harm and fire, as well as criminal mischief and running an entertainment venue without a licence, chief investigator Isara Na Phatthalung said. "He has left the intensive care unit but the doctor has not yet allowed police to read the charges to him," Isara said, adding that police hoped to charge him as the sole suspect in the next few days.

stories.title: Not bye-ing it: Raftery questions qualification rules
stories.summary: Those were the first words out of Jack Raftery's mouth upon stepping off the track after running close to his season’s best in the Men’s 400 metre heats on Day 1 at the European Athletics Championships. For the second time, European Athletics have chosen to not only give top-ranked athletes byes to the semi-finals, but progression to the next round for the unlucky athletes who don’t get a bye is on time only, with no reward for placing highly in your heat. It's an element to the competition which has largely flown under the radar outside of those directly involved in competing but the question needs to be asked - is it fair? The first round of the Men’s 400m saw Raftery finish second but a tense wait followed to see if his time of 47.81 was enough to progress.

stories.title: Triumphant Hayes ready to 'build a new empire' for Cork
stories.summary: Laura Hayes wants to see Cork 'build a new empire' off the back of their All-Ireland Senior Camogie Championship final triumph over Galway at Croke Park. A second-half surge saw the Rebels weather a late Galway fightback as they held out to lift the O'Duffy Cup for the 31st time in their history. The two teams have contested the last three All-Ireland finals, while Cork have competed in every single final since 2021. Hayes, who impressed in the heart of midfield for Cork, wants this victory to be the start of a new era for her side and insisted that they were motivated by starting a new legacy today, rather than revenge for last year's defeat.

stories.title: Corry: Tolka Park has become 'a pressure pot'
stories.summary: Tolka Park has become "a pressure pot" as Shelbourne struggle to find their form even after managerial changes, ex-UCD and Shamrock Rovers midfielder Paul Corry says. Joey O'Brien left Shels on 25 June after a 3-0 defeat to Bohemians which saw them in fifth place in the Men's Premier Division. The club then confirmed a couple of weeks later that Sligo Rovers manager John Russell would be leaving the western outfit to take over but the club has yet to see the famed "new manager bounce." Since Russell's appointment they have dramatically exited the FAI Cup to Kerry FC on penalties and lost two games in the league. They did defeat Nomme Kalju on aggregate to progress in the UEFA Conference League but suffered a 3-1 defeat to Ajax in the next round in a game where it felt like the Dutch side could have easily upped the pressure if they had wanted to. "They can't seem to buy a win in Tolka Park and that result probably comes off the back of a very difficult night over in Amsterdam where the energy must have been sapping through the legs of some of those players. So, it's there for them to get fourth place but do they have it in them? I'm not really sure."

stories.summary: Former rugby league star Brian Carney is confident the Irish sporting public will embrace next year's historic Super League fixtures at the RDS. Warrington Wolves and Wigan Warriors will face off at the newly redeveloped Laya Arena in Dublin on Saturday 24 April 2027, with St Helens taking on Hull FC at the same venue the next day. It is not an unprecedented move. While it will be the first time Super League games have been held in this country, Warrington and Wigan previously met at Shelbourne Park back in 1934, while Wigan returned to the capital in 1995 to face Leeds in a Charity Shield fixture. Corkman Carney forged a highly distinguished career in rugby league, lining out for Hull, Wigan Warriors, Newcastle Knights (in Australia) and Warrington Wolves. stories.title: Cecelia Ahern on returning to romance and writing books for kids
stories.summary: Bestselling author Cecelia Ahern talks to Claire O'Mahony about returning to romance, creating a children's heroine inspired by her daughter, and why she still believes in the impossible. It is, perhaps, the closest Cecelia Ahern comes to explaining the thread that runs through everything she writes, and she has always been drawn to stories that ask readers to suspend disbelief. More than 20 years after PS, I Love You introduced her to millions of readers, that instinct is still strong. This summer, however, she is taking it in two very different directions. Within weeks of each other, she is publishing Love Unlocked, her first full romance in years, and Detective Thingy Majiggy, the first in a new children's series inspired by bedtime reading with her youngest daughter, Blossom, aged 6 – she also has two other children, a daughter Robin and son Sonny who are in their teens. The children's novel began, she says, in the most ordinary of ways. "I think it was reading every night with my daughter," the 44-year-old author says. "I had done it with all of my children who are now teenagers, but I just felt like I'd been engrossed in that world myself with my daughter. Night after night reading books; and she's so into these stories. I had ideas that I was like, 'Yeah, this is the time.'"

stories.title: National emergency as 111 killed in Colombia earthquake
stories.summary: More than 100 people were killed after a powerful earthquake struck western Colombia, toppling buildings, damaging hospitals and infrastructure and trapping people beneath the rubble in the country's strongest earthquake this century. The quake struck just days after Abelardo De La Espriella was sworn in as president, thrusting the new administration into its first major crisis, with memories still fresh of devastating twin earthquakes in neighbouring Venezuela in June. "The national government has all of its capabilities deployed to protect lives, assist affected communities and deliver aid wherever it is needed," he said in a national address at around 1pm local time, upon declaring a national state of emergency and giving a death toll of 111. "The first priority is rescuing the people trapped under the rubble." Mr De La Espriella visited Quibdó, the capital of coastal Chocó province, where he promised rent subsidies for those who have lost homes, and then travelled to Cali, western Colombia's largest city.

stories.title: 3.4% rise in Live Register claimants in July - CSO
stories.summary: There were 191,880 people on the Live Register in July, according to the Central Statistics Office. On a seasonally-adjusted basis, the Live Register figure stood at 174,500 last month, up 1,200 on June. According to the CSO, men made up just over 52% of claimants last month, while 73.4% were Irish. Around 10.7% of claimants were from other countries in the European Union, while roughly 3% were from the United Kingdom.

stories.title: Taoiseach defends Government jet amid navigation concern
stories.summary: Taoiseach Micheál Martin has reiterated the Coalition's defence of the new Government jet but stopped short of denying reports it may have difficulty landing in fog due to the absence of an Israel-made navigational system. The Journal.ie reported this week how the €53 million aircraft was purchased from a French firm without a FalconEye system, which normally sits on the plane's nose and helps it land in fog or other weather conditions that limit visibility, as it was made by an Israeli manufacturer. The Government adopted a policy in 2024 of not awarding Israeli companies defence contracts owing to an advisory opinion from the International Court of Justice against Israeli settlements in the West Bank. Speaking as he visited Fleadh Cheoil na hÉireann in Belfast, Mr Martin insisted the jet "has been very effective".

stories.title: Man to go on trial over murder of rapper Tupac Shakur
stories.summary: A former gang leader will go on trial in Las Vegas today over the decades-old murder of rapper Tupac Shakur, one of America's most high-profile unresolved murders. The proceedings, expected to last a month, will likely not make clear who fired the shots that killed the hip-hop legend on the night of 7 September 1996 while he was in Sin City to see a Mike Tyson boxing match. However, prosecutors aim to show that the defendant, Duane 'Keffe D' Davis, the one-time leader of the south side compton crips, ordered the killing and provided the gun used to kill Mr Shakur in a drive-by shooting. Mr Davis, 63, faces life in prison without parole if convicted.

stories.title: The history of fake tan and Ireland's love affair with it
stories.summary: Beauty and fashion historian Laura Fitzachary joins Brendan O'Connor to give a potted history of fake tan and why Irish people are its biggest fans. Listen back above. For a certain generation of Irish women, slathering on fake tan on a Thursday night was part and parcel of their weekend preparation. The necessary evil of the biscuity smell, the potential for stained sheets and the dreaded scrubbing to remove the last remnants were seen as worth it for a bronzed glow. Although not as central a ritual as before, fake tanning has also taken on a new level of appeal, as more people limit their time in the sun, making "traditional" tanning less likely. But how did fake tan become a beauty staple, and what led to Ireland's unique attachment to it?

stories.title: Agonising deciding frame loss for Hill against Wilson
stories.summary: Aaron Hill suffered an agonising defeat to former world champion Kyren Wilson in the last 32 of the China Open. Hill led 3-1 and 5-4 in the match, while also fouling when approaching the winning line in the final frame. The match, which finished after midnight local time in Taiyuan, was a scrappy affair with Wilson far from his best. The Cork potter hit the highest break of the match, 86, in the second frame.

stories.title: Ruthless Antrim sweep Laois aside in intermediate final
stories.summary: A dominant, ruthless second-half performance that saw Antrim land 13 out of their 16 attempts on goal from the 34th minute onwards, was enough to draw a line under the county's one-year stint outside the Glen Dimplex Senior Championship and send them back up to top tier camogie for 2027. Laois have made immense strides forward over the past couple of seasons, securing success in the league, the Leinster championship and last year’s All-Ireland Premier Junior competition. However after landing the significant scalps of Down and Kerry en route to this final, they found the air far too thin at Croke Park once Antrim turned up the intensity in the second half. Róisín McCormick and Eobha McAllister landed five scores from play apiece over the course of the hour with McCormack firing in the only goal, and on top of that, a string of precision dead-ball strikes that put clear daylight between the sides. Yet when Laois started the second half with three of the first four points after the restart, the smash-and-grab underdog win was there to be seized, albeit the Midlanders were paddling frantically to stay afloat in the contest up to that point.
